notes:
Account: building a paid VS Code extension (copilot-style) that calls Redwood for completions. Key priorities: low-latency streaming for inline suggestions; predictable per-dev quota and graceful degradation when limits hit.

Shorthand / highlights:
- UX: inline, realtime — interruptions are unacceptable; 'blocking' completions must be < 60ms p95 for single-line suggestions.
- Auth: extension will not store long-lived API keys. Plan: short-lived tokens via backend (token exchange), support for SSO/SAML for enterprise installs. Ask: sample JWT workflow and JWKS endpoints.
- Rate limits: per-user burst + org-wide pool. They want client-side backoff guidance + server-side enforcement.
- Model/version pinning: need ability to pin stable model version per release channel (stable/beta) and fallback model on capacity constraints. Rollout API for canary/gradual updates important.
- Offline: MVP should fall back to local heuristics (snippet + fuzzy completion) when network unavailable — product wants a documented 'graceful offline' pattern.
- Security: SOC2 compliance, audit logs for inference calls, optional retention controls (editable retention window), integration with customer KMS for encryption-at-rest.

Quote from CTO (Paraphrase): 'We need copilot responsiveness without surprise bills — and enterprise installs must pass our security gate.'
